A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InVirtuoGen study. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular-generation, PMO optimization, docking, timing, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds conditional-generation experiments, optimization diagnostics, and further PMO comparisons.

M1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds an evaluated conditional-generation variant: a small neural module processes the requested property and adds it to the timestep embedding. The original flow model, sampling rules, GA+PPO optimizer, and adaptive length bandit remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds generation conditioned on requested QED values from 0.30 to 0.90, a distinct requirement from maximizing a property. The training corpora, 23 PMO objectives, fragment-design tasks, and five docking targets remain unchanged. The expanded oracle budget changes protocol rather than dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Graph-GRPO is added as a comparator in both prescreened and non-prescreened PMO comparisons in v2 Tables 6–7, using attributed published scores. Existing comparator membership is retained; the GenMol fragment-generation revisions concern its evaluation procedure and reported results.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3.2 adds a substantially different PMO protocol: up to 100,000 target-oracle calls for preliminary fine-tuning, early stopping, population reset, and then 10,000 calls used for reported AUC. The original fixed-budget experiments remain. Appendix B.2 also replaces GenMol's filtered linker/scaffold evaluation with reported single-step, unfiltered results.

E4.justification: v2 adds validity/uniqueness versus diversity diagnostics in Figure 4 and an optimization-stability case study comparing two otherwise identical runs in Figure 16. These investigate generation trade-offs and seed-dependent policy collapse. The original sampling, loss-weighting, optimization-component, and similarity-constraint analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 16 newly reports individual trajectories labeled seed 0 and seed 2 and specifies identical configurations. Three-run means and standard deviations remain the benchmark reporting practice, including in the new PMO tables; existing ablations remain single-run. No increase in replication for retained experiments is stated.

E6.justification: New PMO Tables 6–7 report totals of 19.552 versus Graph-GRPO's 18.987 without prescreening and 20.269 versus 19.270 with prescreening under the expanded-budget protocol. Fragment results also change: GenMol linker/scaffold quality falls from 21.90 to 4.30 and validity from 100.00 to 16.70 following the protocol replacement. InVirtuoGen's fragment scores receive smaller revisions. Original fixed-budget PMO, docking, and component-ablation scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The probability path, flow constraints, training objectives, length factorization, and optimization equations are retained. v2 adds no mathematical derivation, theorem, proof, or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions paragraph, and conclusion retain the same central claims about refinement-based generation, the quality-diversity frontier, competitive fragment generation, and PMO/docking performance. Added experiments and changed emphasis do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation through arguments about soft prompting, quality versus validity, GenMol filtering, and oracle-budget accounting. Appendix B.3.3 newly attributes possible policy collapse to excessive exploitation and identifies stabilization as future work. However, its claim that the collapsing run achieves higher AUC conflicts with Figure 16's labeled curves.

D1.justification: Section 6 newly specifies replication scripts, a Dockerfile, and instructions beyond v1's general code/checkpoint release statement. Appendices B.3.2 and B.5 document the preliminary fine-tuning/reset procedure and conditioning-module integration. Existing architecture, training hyperparameters, and timing details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references on Graph-GRPO, conditional molecular generation, discrete guidance, and reinforcement-learning stabilization. It also revises the GenMol comparison from predefined reaction templates to fixed dummy attachment points and introduces a focused critique of oracle-budget conventions. The broader research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 adds Sections 2.3 and 6, rewrites the fragment-generation discussion, and moves its detailed benchmark description into Appendix B.2. New appendix subsections and publication disclosures extend the structure, while most original prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands through validity/uniqueness trade-off panels, a dual-axis seed-stability plot, conditional-QED distributions, and two full PMO comparison tables. The fragment-results table moves from main-text Table 1 to appendix Table 4 with a revised caption. Existing figures are retained, with some relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v2 improves experimental context by explaining the GenMol filtering mismatch, separating the larger-budget PMO comparison, and documenting conditional control and optimization instability. These provide useful evidence beyond v1 while preserving its core results. The gains are tempered by introduced inconsistencies: Figure 16 contradicts the claimed AUC ordering, and Table 4's caption incorrectly identifies scaffold decoration as sharing linker-design results. Overall, the added transparency and evidence support a limited net improvement.
